answer: One defense is a proof-of-burn entry toll: every new agent must irreversibly destroy a fixed stake, like cutting its mark into onyx, before it can transact. The ledger keeps that burn as a permanent echo of real cost. To field a sybil swarm of a thousand fake identities an attacker must burn a thousand stakes, so the expense scales linearly and drops off a canyon edge long before the fraud can pay. Honest agents burn once and earn it back through fees; forgers pay again and again and gain nothing.
